sampling_method: This is the ECCV/Springer LNCS proceedings layout (single column, running header alternating by page parity), so reading order is simply page order, top-to-bottom, with no two-column interleaving to resolve. Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in that order, row-major within a table and left-to-right across that row's own-result columns only, giving a population of 1..137. Ownership throughout is settled by explicit citation brackets rather than inference: Table 1's 'Generalist SOTA' and 'Specialist SOTA' columns carry a bracketed citation on every printed entry ([57],[19],[55],[19],[55],[58] and [61],[38],[38] respectively) and are baselines throughout, while its 'BiT-L' column carries none and is own; Table 3's first row is explicitly 'RetinaNet [33]' with the caption naming it 'the literature baseline', while the three 'RetinaNet (BiT-S/M/L)' rows are the authors' own backbones run through the same detector. Tables 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 contain no baseline row at all -- every printed cell is BiT's own model (BiT-S/M/L, or the Table 4/5 normalization ablation the authors trained from scratch) -- so ownership there is not a judgement call. Table 2's 'Improvement' row is excluded entirely: it is a delta (BiT-M minus BiT-S) and both absolute rows it is computed from are printed in the very same table, so counting it would double the same six measurements. The same rule cuts the other way twice: Sec. 3.7's 'a 1.5 point improvement in Average Precision (AP)' and 'improves performance by 0.6 points' are counted (2 cells) because their absolutes (41.7/43.2/43.8) are in Table 3, a different location; and Sec. 4.3's 'a performance drop of 5.4% on ILSVRC-2012 top-1 accuracy' is counted (1 cell) because its absolutes (75.6, 70.2) are in Table 4, a different location. Where an absolute is printed beside a delta in the same breath, only the absolute counts: Sec. 3.6's 'achieving unprecedented top-5 accuracy of 80.0%, an almost 25% absolute improvement over the previous state-of-the-art' counts only the 80.0% (a restatement of Table 6's R152x4/L, Resize&Crop, Top-5 cell), and Appendix A's '78.72%, an absolute improvement of 2.43% over 76.29%' counts the two absolutes (78.72% is new; 76.29% restates Table 1's VTAB row) but not the 2.43% delta between them. Consistent with counting each printed instance rather than deduplicating by underlying quantity, the abstract's five headline figures (87.5%, 99.4%, 76.3%, 76.8%, 97.0%) are rounded restatements of numbers printed more precisely elsewhere (Table 1's BiT-L column; Figure 2's un-printed few-shot curves) but are themselves fresh printed digit strings at a new location, so all five are counted at the Abstract. Excluded as not a specific transcribable value: Discussion's 'around half of the model's mistakes on CIFAR-10 are due to ambiguity or label noise' (page 15) -- an approximation with no printed digit, unlike the same paragraph's precise '19.21%' two sentences later, which is counted. Excluded as dataset_statistic throughout: JFT-300M/ImageNet-21k/ILSVRC-2012 image and class counts (Secs. 2.1, 3.1, Related Work), and Table 7's three 'Dups' columns (near-duplicate-image counts, not a performance outcome) -- the 'Full' and 'Dedup' columns beside them are accuracy results and counted. Figures 1 through 15 without exception carry only axis-tick calibration, legend text or method-name labels (e.g. Figure 3's 'VIVI-Ex-100%', a citation's own name) and print no per-point data value, so every figure location is 0; the numeric content of Figures 4 and 10 lives instead in Tables 3 and 6, which are counted there. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 138), 15) drew {1, 2, 12, 13, 14, 25, 29, 70, 79, 83, 91, 99, 107, 108, 122}; each label below records its draw as frame_index. Four draws (1, 2, 25, 29) land on sequential prose values with no row/column ambiguity and needed no image. The other eleven land in Table 2 (page 6), Table 6 (page 21) and Table 7 (page 22); page images for exactly those three pages were rendered from the same unchanged PDF and checked against every row/column attribution below -- no page holds a drawn cell outside {1, 6, 7, 21, 22}, so no other page was rendered.
